newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan raises sugarcane support price.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan raises sugarcane support price.

text.p: Pakistan, which has imported more than 500,000 tonnes of sugar this financial year, has raised the sugarcane support price to boost domestic output and save foreign exchange, officials said on Wednesday.
"The raise will help higher production of sugar next year," Khadim Ali Qazilbash, secretary general of the Pakistan Sugar Mills Association, told Reuters on Wednesday.

The government on Tuesday increased the support price for the 1997/98 (July-June) crop to 35 rupees from 24 per 40 kg last year for Punjab and North West Frontier provinces, and to 36 rupees from 24.50 in Sindh and Balochistan provinces.
Planting increased after some mills paid 45 rupees per 40 kg for sugarcane this year, compared to less than 35 rupees last year.
Qailbash said mill owners were expecting output of three million tonnes of refined crystal white sugar and one million tonnes of partially refined sugar, known as gur, in 1997/98.
In 1996/97, mill owners had hoped to produce 2.65 million tonnes, but output had reached only 2.32 million tonnes by April 15 due to a shortage of sugarcane.
Qazilbash said production was likely to reach 2.38 million tonnes by the end of the year, compared to 2.47 million tonnes in 1995/96 and three million tonnes in 1994/95.

Sugar consumption is likely to rise to 2.85 million tonnes in 1997/98, up from an expected 2.7 million tonnes this year, he said. The forecast includes 1.8 million tonnes for domestic use, 900,000 tonnes for industry and 150,000 tonnes for Afghanistan.
"We think there will be no need for sugar imports next year," Qazilbash said.
He said 68 out of 75 mills would be operating this year, with the rest closed because of financial problems. The mills have a combined capacity of five million tonnes a year.

Pakistan imported 518,976 tonnes of sugar worth $197 million in the first 10 months of 1996/97 (July-June) compared to a negligible 2,759 tonnes in the year-ago period. It plans to import 50,000 tonnes in the next two months.
In April, sugar imports rose to 34,388 tonnes worth $12 million compared to 16,134 tonnes worth $6 million in March.
